title: The Environment is the only place tools execute
context: The AI SDK will happily execute tools itself if a tool is declared with an execute function. That would put tool execution inside the contestant, where the harness cannot observe it.
decision: Contestants return tool CALLS and never run them. Tools are declared without execute and the agent is capped at stepCountIs(1); the Environment executes every call.
consequences: ToolLoopAgent is used as a single-step agent. In exchange, DB hashing, Layer-1 event capture, and parity between a local model and a deployed HTTP endpoint are all possible.

title: Cache-first prompt layout: stable prefix first, variable content last
context: Prompt caching is a prefix match. One changed byte anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. A benchmark running tens of thousands of conversations pays for that mistake on every call.
decision: Assemble every prompt stable-prefix-first: system/policy, tool schemas, docs, conversation so far, this turn. No timestamp, UUID, turn counter or session id ever goes in a system prompt.
consequences: Per-turn context must go in the message list, never interpolated into the system prompt. Prompt hashes are recorded in the manifest so a drift is detectable.

title: Split "can place a breakpoint" from "reports cache reads"
context: The cache probe gated on supportsExplicitCaching, using "can the caller place a breakpoint?" to answer "is caching measurable at all?". It therefore skipped every provider that caches automatically.
decision: Two flags. supportsExplicitCaching drives only whether providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl is sent. reportsCacheReads drives whether the probe runs.
consequences: reportsCacheReads: false means unverified, not absent. --force-cache-check probes anyway; flip the flag once a real run reports.

title: OpenAI needs a stable promptCacheKey, or nothing caches
context: Four byte-identical 30,641-token OpenAI calls read zero cached tokens. The prefix layout was correct; the requests were being routed to different backends.
decision: Send a stable promptCacheKey for kind === openai, derived from the system-prompt hash and truncated to 64 chars, from one helper shared by the probe and the conversation paths.
consequences: Placement is automatic on OpenAI but routing is not. Without the key a sweep pays list price while believing the cache lever is engaged.

title: Do not send promptCacheOptions mode:explicit
context: The AI SDK exposes promptCacheOptions { mode: explicit } for OpenAI, which would make OpenAI caching deterministic like Anthropic. gpt-4.1-mini rejects it.
decision: Do not send prompt_cache_options. Re-check per model before assuming a newer contestant supports it.
consequences: OpenAI caching stays best-effort, so a miss there is INCONCLUSIVE rather than a proven defect. An SDK type surface is not proof a model accepts the field.

title: No provider honours seed; live reproducibility rests elsewhere
context: scenario.seed is passed on every call and recorded in the manifest, but Anthropic, OpenAI and Google all report seed as unsupported and sample freely.
decision: Keep passing and recording the seed, but never claim live runs are reproducible because of it. Reproducibility rests on pinned model version, prompt hashes, gold-DB hash and published transcripts.
consequences: Only the offline smoke is byte-reproducible. K (trials per scenario) is the real lever against variance, so per-scenario variance monitoring matters more, not less.

title: A gate check states only what it proves
context: pnpm smoke printed "G1 PASSED" after a run that makes zero model calls, but G1 has two clauses and the second requires a live call. Half a gate read as a whole one.
decision: Every gate check reports only the clause it actually exercised, and names the command that covers the rest. No check asserts a global gate state it cannot observe.
consequences: Output is wordier. In exchange a green check cannot be mistaken for a met gate.

title: Two decision logs, split by leakage risk
context: Decisions were accumulating in the project working notes, which is a working guide that gets rewritten. A benchmark also cannot publish every decision it makes without leaking what it scores.
decision: Append-only ADR log in docs/decisions/ (public, committed) and docs/decisions-private/ (gitignored). Public ADRs may never cite private ones, in either direction of content or id.
consequences: Two places to look. the working notes become a guide that points at the log rather than a growing decision record.

title: Pin floating model aliases to dated snapshots
context: No provider honours seed (ADR-0006), so a silently repointed floating alias is the dominant remaining reproducibility risk: half a sweep could run against a different model with nothing in the manifest or the response to show it.
decision: Resolve floating aliases to dated snapshots at parseModelRef. Record both the snapshot and the requested ref in the manifest with a versionPinned flag. Pins are copied from the installed SDK model-id unions; an alias with no verified snapshot is left unpinned and warned about rather than guessed.
consequences: A result claiming reproducibility needs versionPinned true on every model; gemini-2.5-flash is currently the gap. MODEL_PINS goes stale like the price table and must be re-verified at freeze.

title: No application framework in the harness; NestJS is the product stack
context: NestJS appears three times in the planning material and never as the harness stack: once in a superseded 2026-07-30 report, once as part of the rationale for choosing TypeScript (the future WhatsApp product is Node/NestJS), and once in the productization path. The scattered answer makes the question recur.
decision: The harness has no application framework. It is a library plus two CLI entry points. NestJS enters only when the API and dashboard are built, and that service consumes the engine as a library rather than absorbing it.
consequences: A server framework stays out of the dependency graph of an artifact whose value is being auditable and reproducible. Test for any future proposal: has the harness started serving requests? If not, no.

title: AI SDK v6 surface: five places reality differed from the plan
context: The plan named ToolLoopAgent, stopWhen, stepCountIs and tool(), all of which exist in ai@6.0.239. Five details differ from what the plan assumed, and each one silently changes behaviour rather than failing loudly.
decision: Record the five deviations: inputSchema not parameters; tools declared without execute; cache tokens are provider-agnostic via inputTokenDetails; Anthropic cacheControl is a call-level option; tool results use output: { type, value }; and the six ZodObject schemas need widening at the tool() call.
consequences: ToolLoopAgent is deliberately used as a single-step agent. Anyone upgrading the SDK should re-check all five, because most would fail as wrong behaviour rather than as a type error.

title: Gate sampling params per model instead of discovering the 400 mid-sweep
context: Newer Anthropic models reject temperature / top_p / top_k outright with HTTP 400. A sweep that sets them unconditionally dies on turn one, after the scenario has been set up and paid for.
decision: supportsSamplingParams(ref) is checked before any sampling parameter is set. Unsupported models simply do not receive them.
consequences: Those models run at provider defaults, so temperature is not a controlled variable for them - worth stating in any write-up that reports temperatures per model.

title: The price table refuses to invent a number
context: A cost model is a headline claim in a benchmark paper. The easy failure is a missing price silently costing $0, which makes an unpriced sweep look cheap rather than unmeasured.
decision: An unknown model yields { usd: null, priced: false } and increments unpricedCalls. Entries carry a confidence flag and a lastVerified date; unverifiable rates are explicit placeholders rather than plausible guesses.
consequences: A run can report tokens without dollars, which is the honest outcome. Every entry must be re-verified at freeze.

title: Personas are public; scenarios are persona-bound instance files split at authoring time
context: Phase 1 needed three shape decisions before authoring: persona publicness, whether instances are runtime crossings or authored files, and when the public/private split is decided.
decision: Personas ship publicly (hidden fields are runtime-hidden from the contestant, not from readers). Each scenario file is one persona-bound instance stating that pairing's exact ground truth. The pool tag is authored in, private instances are written straight into private-pool/, and the loader treats that directory as optional. Floors and balance rules are enforced by pnpm gate:phase1.
consequences: Per-pair ground truth becomes possible (the Phase 1 gate requires it) at the cost of more files than a crossing matrix. When in doubt scenarios are authored private, because public-to-private is a history rewrite.

title: Layer-1 checks fire only on quotable, context-anchored evidence
context: The 4.1 checks hide interpretation problems: what counts as a stated price in free text, what tolerance-0 means for rounded lakh/crore quotes, and where per-scenario oracle data comes from. G3 demands zero false fires on clean transcripts.
decision: Extraction requires explicit context (currency/sqft/km/possession/percent-context markers); matching is tolerance-0 at the claim's stated precision; ground money includes derivable cost-sheet lines and excludes EMI arithmetic; the L1.5 oracle derives from the declared expectedOutcome; spurious-escalation fires only in trap-free scenarios; templates, thresholds and wordlists are frozen in versioned config (I3); log_qualification.budgetInr became optional so honesty is expressible.
consequences: Recall is deliberately bounded - uncontexted claims are the judge panel's to catch. Tightening extractors must re-clear G3 (20/20 caught, 0/16 false fires) and bump CHECK_CONFIG_VERSION.

title: OpenRouter routing is not behaviour-neutral: pin the host, use the chat surface
context: The Phase 3 pilot routed Qwen buyers through OpenRouter, which load-balances across upstream hosts with different prices, quantisations and capabilities. Groq rejects every buyer-opener conversation (assistant prefill), and the Responses translation layer 400'd whole batches as endpoint metadata shifted, then passed the same requests minutes later; a thinking model's text came back empty through it.
decision: An @Host ref suffix (openrouter/qwen/qwen3-32b@DeepInfra) injects OpenRouter's provider routing-preference field with allow_fallbacks:false via a custom fetch; the manifest records routingPin while modelId stays bare for pricing. OpenAI-compatible gateways use .chat() instead of the default Responses callable. Sweeps retry an infra-errored conversation once from a fresh clone, with retriedConversations in the manifest.
consequences: Comparative runs hold host and surface constant, so probe deltas measure the model, not the router. A pinned host that is down fails loudly rather than silently substituting. OpenRouter cache-read reporting must be re-verified on the chat path before relying on buyer-side cache figures.

title: Buyer probes: frame breaks are zero-tolerance, scripted values are sanctioned, the human leg runs blind
context: Phase 3 validates the buyer simulator the agent scores inherit. The Master Plan names the probes but not their operational definitions; the pilot surfaced scripted-opening ceilings being counted as leaks, agent-closed cold leads being scored against the buyer, and the 32B buyer pasting its private simulation-reminder into 16 replies across 8/20 conversations - caught by human review, not by any machine probe.
decision: pnpm probes scores leakage as a stated hidden reservation value (L1 extraction discipline, volunteered vs elicited split, gate on volunteered <=5% of turns) with scenario-scripted values sanctioned; a P09 walk-away counts as executed on any no-booking quiet close (buyer STOP or flow-ending tool); frame breaks are their own zero-tolerance probe, with echoed blocks stripped before leak extraction; the human obviously-an-AI leg runs blind with model identity hidden and a <=20% flag gate per model.
consequences: Pilot verdict 2026-08-20: Qwen3-235B passes every gate and is the confirmed primary; Qwen3-32B fails frame breaks, premature stops and the blind review (5/5 flagged) and is only a disclosed sensitivity slice. Human ratings are archived beside the runs; the single-rater protocol is explicitly not the Phase 7 three-rater validation.

title: Judge scaffolding: offline-first, quote-then-verdict enforced structurally, polarity normalised once
context: Phase 5 runs the cross-family panel over the calibration set and gates on G8/G8a kappa, inter-judge alpha and seeded-fail recall. The scaffolding was built before the human labels exist; the plan leaves the output contract, retry behaviour and item polarity to the implementer, small judges exhibit truth bias on bare booleans, and CP items are violation-worded while F/SE/CQ are criterion-worded - a polarity mistake silently inverts every kappa.
decision: Model calls sit behind a one-function seam so the whole pipeline runs offline for $0 (dry-run prices a pass without an API call); quote-then-verdict is a schema rule with one retry and structured-error storage; polarity is normalised in exactly one module; the judge system block is byte-identical per (judge, dimension) and blind to band/source/provenance; agreement statistics come only from stats-bridge with ties dropping units; panel refs are declared but unpinned and unpriced until the Phase-5 cache smoke; batch billing is deferred in favour of interactive-with-cache.
consequences: When labels arrive the remaining machine work is verify refs/prices at smoke, judge:calibration, judge:agreement, gate:phase5. Verdict files are resumable per (judge, case, dimension); --retest gives test-retest. The gate reports honest UNMET floors today. Judgments live under calibration/ and inherit its gitignore.

title: Phases 6-10 scaffolded machine-first: every gate is code before any run is paid for
context: After the judge scaffold, the remaining phases split into machine work (run rules, judging runs, composite scoring, monitoring gates, sampling, leakage audit) and human work. Building the machine parts before any main-run spend makes every section-11 gate an executable check and the paid phases 'run the command'.
decision: D5 lives in the sweep (--trials-rule=d5) with pnpm matrix as a spend-free planner; I9's Hinglish floor is read as the FAMILY floor (>=30 hinglish_variant - honestly UNMET at 22, +8 to author); judging runs reuses the calibration machinery with the 4.1 gating rule enforced at load; section 4.3 is implemented literally as pure functions with the G15 D4-to-pass^k CI fixture; Wilson is closed-form golden-tested and the bootstrap uses a seeded xorshift32; Phase 7 reuses the labeling stack with blind cal_hv cases and a never-served mapping.json; G16 is a mechanical git-history audit (first run: 45 ids x 58 commits, clean); Phase 9 gets no scaffold.
consequences: Paid path: author 8 Hinglish instances -> judge smoke -> d5 sweeps -> judge:run -> gate:phase6 -> leaderboard -> sample:human -> 3 raters -> gate:phase7 -> gate:leakage. The leaderboard counts unjudged conversations as coverage debt, never silently scoring them; G13 names the instances to raise K on.

title: Buyer guardrails hardened with an anti-repetition mandate after the G6 pilot audit
context: The G6 manual audit of all 20 primary-pilot transcripts (235B, open-card via pnpm audit:g6) landed at 4 minor / 0 critical = 20%, inside the 16-22% band - MET. The minors cluster into two mechanisms: repetition loops (2 cases, up to 5 consecutive re-sends; SPASM-style drift with no covering guardrail) and fabrication slips (2 cases violating an instruction that already exists). Both initially-marked criticals were withdrawn on review - the rater had misread scripted or agent-side endings as buyer deviations.
decision: Add one anti-repetition line to the GharBench-authored WhatsApp-register section (test-pinned; tau2-lifted sections stay byte-faithful). No new line for fabrication - restating a violated instruction dilutes the prompt without evidence. The G6 UI now shows termination source, expected outcome, mustHold, walk-away triggers, armed-trap scripts and judge-aligned tN turn numbers; the same affordances go into the Phase 7 rater instructions.
consequences: Buyer prompt sha changes relative to the pilot (manifests record buyerPromptSha256, so the generations stay distinguishable); pilot verdicts remain valid for the prompt they ran; Phase 6 runs hardened. Re-measure repetition at the Phase 6 G6 spot-check. Human notes and judge evidence share one turn-numbering scheme, which Phase 7 adjudication depends on.

title: Calibration labeler hardened: opaque case aliases and violation-polarity buttons
context: The first labeling sitting stalled on an undocumented task, and reviewing the tool surfaced two real defects: case ids encode provenance (cal_syn_pass_*, cal_adv_*, cal_real_<contestant>_*) and were displayed in the sidebar, handing the rater the expected answer; and CP items are violation-worded with stored met = 'the violation happened' (polarity.ts) while the button said 'Met' in pass-green - a rater reading Met = complied would silently invert every compliance label. Zero labels existed at discovery.
decision: The rater-facing API speaks positional per-rater aliases only (c017 = 17th case in the deterministic shuffle); redactCase drops caseId alongside band/source/provenance; saves post the alias and the server maps back, still writing label files under real ids (no downstream change). CP items render as 'Violation - happened' (red) / 'No violation' (green); stored values unchanged, polarity.ts stays the single flip point. An instructions panel states the goal, tie semantics and evidence-by-turn convention; bubbles carry judge-aligned tN numbers. Pinned in tests/calibrationLabeler.test.ts.
consequences: Blindness holds end to end at the API surface (fetch by real id is a 404); Phase 7 inherits the same UI via --dir; colleague raters need no polarity briefing. Threat model is anti-priming for cooperative raters, not anti-adversary.

title: The labeler shows the judge's source documents and the gold DB
context: F1-F5 and several CP items are judged 'against the source documents', but the labeler showed none - no way to verify a quoted price, amenity claim, or slot availability. The LLM judges receive the full document set verbatim in their system block, so the human answer key was less informed than the judges it calibrates; grounding items were only answerable from memory.
decision: /api/reference serves the rater the same 11 corpus documents the judges get (byte-parity with loadSourceDocuments test-pinned) plus a gold-DB digest: 32 units (carpet vs SBU, price, status), 14 site-visit slots (capacity/booked), agent policy (max discount, token, prohibited promises), project facts. UI renders a tabbed Ground-truth panel above the transcript; every grounding-dependent item carries a 'check:' hint naming the deciding tab or document; conduct-rule CP items are marked as needing no document. Units/Slots tabs carry a caveat: DB is start-of-conversation state, bookings mid-chat legitimately change it, prefer Can't-decide where the agent could have learned different state.
consequences: The corpus is identical across cases so blindness is untouched; the human key is now at least as informed as the judges (DB digest makes it slightly more - the right direction for an answer key); Layer-1 stays the authority on tool-level fabrication; Phase 7 inherits via --dir.

title: Pre-run pipeline hardening: contestant-aware check reports and gate completeness floors
context: Before paid phases, a high-effort review of src/run + src/judge + src/metrics plus a runtime audit of every stage command found ten confirmed defects. Worst: check reports keyed by conversationId alone (scenario#trial, identical across contestants), so multi-contestant sweeps scored/gated/judged every contestant against the LAST contestant's Layer-1 report. Also: missing checks.jsonl entries scored programmatically perfect and ungated; one surviving judge verdict recorded as scored 0.0 instead of coverage debt; --max-usd NaN silently disabled the budget cap; evidence 'none' variants smuggled unevidenced VIOLATIONs past the quote-then-verdict guard; gate:phase6 could print MET with its variance floor never pushed.
decision: CheckReport gains required contestantId; new src/run/checkReports.ts CheckReportIndex is the single reader (judgeRun, leaderboard, calibrationBuild, humanSample), normalising contestant: prefixes and @Host pins; ambiguous legacy multi-contestant files fail loudly (regenerate with pnpm checks), single-contestant legacy still loads. Leaderboard gains unchecked/unjudged statuses never folded into scores; 2-verdict panel minimum; gate:phase7 gains a panel-coverage floor; every gate floor pushed on every path; --max-usd NaN-validated in sweep+judgeRun; retried conversations merge both attempts into costs.json; no-evidence predicate hardened at schema+judge sites; seeded-bootstrap divisor + percentile index fixed in metrics/ci.ts; labeler alias map frozen at startup.
consequences: Multi-contestant attribution now correct - this error class would have invalidated the leaderboard invisibly. Old multi-contestant runs (the calibration sweeps) must re-run pnpm checks before scoring. Two findings flagged not fixed (measurement design): judge prompt shape differs between synthetic and real calibration cases (tell on seeded recall), and conduct-only judgeApplicability lists identify 4 of 8 synthetic known-fails - decide both before judge:calibration.

title: Calibration judging: uniform prompt shape and no conduct-only item lists
context: Two ADR-0024 flags made seeded cases distinguishable exactly where judge sensitivity is measured: real-provenance cases got a scenario card + Layer-1 results while the 18 seeded cases got neither (every seeded prompt visibly read 'no card + PROGRAMMATIC RESULTS unavailable' - a 100% tell on seeded recall), and 4 of 8 known-fails carried conduct-only compliance lists occurring in 0/118 real cases.
decision: One uniform minimal prompt shape for every calibration case (toCalibrationJudgeable): no scenario card, no Layer-1, regardless of provenance - chosen over fabricating cards/L1 stubs because it fabricates nothing and matches the human labeler's information set, the right basis for G8. Run-mode judging keeps card+L1 (uniform there; richer context at deployment only helps - calibration validates the conservative lower bound). Every seed's compliance list now includes >=1 doc-verifiable item (CP1-CP4, CP6, CP9) resembling real compositions; added items are expected-pass, violatedItems unchanged. Both rules test-pinned.
consequences: Cases regenerated; ids unchanged, slice-50 intact, sidecars consistent, 0 labels existed. Verified 0 conduct-only lists across 136 cases; dry-run estimate dropped $5.84->$5.65. Honest residual: CP7/CP8 still occur only in seeded cases (no sweep scenario armed those traps) - judges are stateless per call so no in-prompt tell remains, but the item-level correlation is recorded; a future calibration refresh with armed CP7/CP8 scenarios removes it.

title: Shared rubric interpretation notes; disclosed rater-baseline adjudication
context: Labeling case 1 surfaced a rubric ambiguity (SE5 when the buyer ends the conversation). Answering the rater in chat creates guidance the judges never see - asymmetric information skewing G8. The rater also asked for feedback on their first label to set a baseline; answer-feedback mid-labeling risks contaminating the blind protocol.
decision: data/judge-items.json (1.1.0) gains interpretationNotes - GharBench clarifications rendered from ONE source to both the labeler UI and the owning dimension's judge system block, test-pinned on both surfaces. First note: SE5's buyer-ended rule (buyer closing is not itself a failure; judge the best step secured or cleanly attempted; graceful close of a non-advancing buyer counts; walk-away quality belongs to SA2). Separately: one disclosed baseline adjudication - the assistant second-read the rater's first saved case (transcript + gold DB, evidence-cited), recorded in calibration/protocol-notes.md; no band/source revealed; answers remain the rater's own.
consequences: Future ambiguities are resolved by adding a shared note, never chat-only guidance. Judge system prompt grows (no judgments existed - no sha continuity broken); labeler server restart needed on rubric change. Exactly 1/136 cases carries a disclosed assisted-baseline flag, droppable in a Phase 5 sensitivity check.

title: Every calibration case records who ended the conversation
context: A rater could not tell whether a transcript ending on a buyer question meant the agent went silent or closed the lead: an agent flow-ending tool action has no text bubble, so in the buyer-view projection an agent close looks identical to ignoring the buyer - the exact misread behind both false G6 pilot criticals (ADR-0021). It affects 60 of 136 calibration cases (44%): 69 buyer / 60 agent / 7 harness.
decision: CalibrationCase gains required endedBy: buyer|agent|harness, populated by calibrationBuild and humanSample from terminationReason via the exported terminationSource mapping; authored per-seed for the 18 synthetics; the 118 real cases migrated from source-run transcripts (118/118, 0 problems). Symmetric per ADR-0026: labeler shows an ended-by chip + guide bullet; the judge user turn carries endedBy plus a fixed explainer, in calibration and run modes alike.
consequences: 'Did the agent ignore the last question' is decidable: agent = the reply was a tool action; harness = the cut-off is not the agent's fault; buyer = walked. What that implies for CQ3/SE5 stays the rater's call. Required schema means a future builder that forgets the field fails loudly; Phase 7 inherits automatically; no judgments existed so no prompt continuity broke.

title: Buyer scaffolding leaks: 17 calibration cases purged, leak screen added, buyer prompt hardened
context: A rater found <simulation-reminder> text inside a buyer message. Scan of all 136 cases: 17 real cases (38 buyer messages) contain a reminder-style block the 235B buyer wrote ITSELF - not an echo of the harness block but a self-authored imitation carrying the hidden brief verbatim (budget ceiling, stretch rule, walk-away triggers) - handed to the agent, voiding those conversations for scoring. The frame-break probe was only ever run on the pilot (235B: 0/20); the calibration sweeps were never probed and calibration:build had no screen. Leak rate there ~13% - the pilot's clean 20 was favourable sampling.
decision: Purged the 17 (136 -> 119; size floor is 100-300, all family/band floors still MET; one saved label archived under labels/archived-purged, not counted). buyerLeakMarker screen added to calibrationBuild AND humanSample (reminder tags, card vocabulary, stop-token text, <scenario>, '(no reply yet)'; 0 false positives over the surviving 119; test-pinned). Buyer prompt hardened: 'Never write such a block yourself... Your reply is only the WhatsApp message text' (test-pinned; sha changes, still pre-Phase 6). Runbook rule: every sweep runs pnpm probes before anything consumes it.
consequences: 50-slice regenerated (7 of its cases were purged; colleagues had not started); rater case numbering shifts (positional aliases). The 235B leak propensity is a documented finding: 0/20 pilot vs ~13% calibration sweeps - re-measure after hardening at the Phase 6 G6 spot-check; if material, revisit the simulator decision on a bigger sample. A top-up sweep under the hardened prompt can restore n toward 136 if Phase 5 wants it.

title: Agent-ended cases carry the closing tool; the answer key shows the agent's full capability surface
context: endedBy=agent was ambiguous between log_qualification (lead logged and closed) and escalate_to_human (handoff) - opposite meanings for SE5/CP10. And a rater could not answer 'does the agent even have such a facility?' (claimed unit holds, claimed NOCs): tool calls are invisible in the transcript, and the tool roster and sendable-asset list were not on screen.
decision: endedByTool required exactly when endedBy=agent (schema superRefine), derived from the last successful flow-ending tool result (closingTool in calibrationBuild, shared with judgeRun run-mode and humanSample); shown to raters (chip) and judges (card field + explainer) alike. Backfilled across all 119 cases (53 agent-ended: 44 escalate / 6 log real, 3 authored seed log). Reference panel gains the six-tool roster (from TOOL_SPECS) and the 17-asset sendable list with the no-hold-facility / closed-asset-list rules inline (ADR-0023 extension).
consequences: Mid-conversation tool truth stays Layer-1 work (ADR-0025 stands); slot/facility EXISTENCE cannot change mid-chat and needs no tie. Case files changed by one line each - labels and alias order unaffected. Paper note: 44/50 real agent closes are escalations.

title: SISTER work order: judge-robustness machinery, clustered CIs, canary, release hygiene
context: External research pass (2026-08-28) compared GharBench to best-in-class benchmark practice (SISTER, MT-Bench, PoLL, tau-bench, HAL, LiveBench, NeurIPS D&B rules). Headline: judge ablations must exist BEFORE the paid Phase 6 run - retrofitting order-robustness after ~5,300 judged conversations means paying twice. SISTER's Zenodo records verified live: software 10.5281/zenodo.21951541, dataset 10.5281/zenodo.21954790 (v0.1.0, 2026-08-15, dataset creator Singh alone); no venue publication exists yet.
decision: Item-order ablation adapted to rubric judging (no A/B pair exists): --item-order=reversed emits to judgments-reversed/, prompts test-pinned as line-permutations. Ablation metrics built as pure functions (flip rate, self-preference with familyOverlap guard, leave-one-judge-out, length bias). clusteredBootstrapMeanCi in TS ci.ts (deviation from work order: consumers are TS; stats-bridge rule covers agreement stats only). Canary: fresh GUID stamped into all 45 private files via pnpm canary:stamp, GUID only in private-pool/CANARY.md; no prompt builder reads the field (test-pinned - a canary sent to a provider could fire the probe without a real leak). Evidence-first audit recorded as ALREADY implemented (quote-then-verdict per item). CITATION.cff, MIT/CC-BY-4.0 licence split, CHANGELOG, paper/refs.bib with verified BibTeX + permission-gated acknowledgment stub. Deferred pre-registered: Holm/effect sizes/Gwet AC1 at Phase 8; Croissant+RAI (a D&B submission gate), datasheet, annotator-pay, leaderboard policy at Phase 10.
consequences: Phase 6 budget covers the ablations by emitting nothing extra; default itemOrder=original is byte-identical so existing shas/verdicts hold. Phase 8 reports must use the clustered CI (naive CIs on K-trial data are too narrow). Ack naming Anshuman Singh publishes only on written permission. If a judge family ever overlaps a contestant family, the self-preference table + recusal thresholds in docs/judge-protocol.md become mandatory.

title: Operational profile: latency published as serving telemetry, never scored
context: Vendors deciding on an agent model care how long a lead waits; on WhatsApp full-response latency IS the UX (no streaming). latencyMs was always metered but costs.json only kept per-conversation aggregates mixing buyer and contestant calls. Latency measures the provider serving stack on the run date, not the checkpoint - unreproducible from pins, so it must not enter the composite, a ranking, or a gate.
decision: Sweep persists an ordered per-call `calls` array (role, modelId, latencyMs, outputTokens, cacheHit) per conversation; call order carries reply boundaries (one turn() = one model call, so a buyer-visible reply = the run of consecutive contestant calls between buyer calls). Pure src/metrics/operationalProfile.ts computes per-reply and per-call p50/p95/mean/max (ci.ts order-statistic convention), calls/reply and output tokens/sec. The leaderboard prints it as a separate descriptive section and embeds OPERATIONAL_PROFILE_NOTE verbatim in the JSON; pre-ADR-0031 runs read 'latency telemetry unavailable'. Latency-blindness of composite.ts, passk.ts and the judge stack is test-pinned.
consequences: Reply p50/p95 and tok/s appear beside $/conv, labeled measured-on-date serving telemetry. Paper latency claims must carry run date and provider routing and never appear in a ranking sentence. Batch-billed runs (deferred, ADR-0019) would make the profile meaningless - suppress or label before reading. Existing runs are not migrated.
reversible: yes - drop the calls array and the leaderboard section; scoring is untouched by construction

title: Judge panel serving ids verified; all three judges route through OpenRouter, Mistral slot resolves to Medium 3.5
context: ADR-0019 left the §6.4 panel refs as best guesses to confirm at the Phase-5 smoke. With the answer key complete (119/119, gate:phase4 MET) the paid pass is next. The account has no funded xAI or Mistral key (both blank in .env, direct APIs return 401); OpenRouter is funded and publishes per-endpoint prices. Mistral Large 3 has zero OpenRouter endpoints and its $0.50/$1.50 price cannot be confirmed.
decision: Route all three judges through OpenRouter with @Host pins: openrouter/x-ai/grok-4.3@xAI, openrouter/mistralai/mistral-medium-3-5@Mistral, openrouter/meta-llama/llama-4-maverick@DeepInfra. The Mistral slot resolves to Medium 3.5 under the Master Plan §6.4 I7 rule; Large 3 is the named reserve. Prices recorded as verified from the pinned host endpoint entries; upstream dated names (grok-4.3-20260430, mistral-medium-3.5-20260430) are the pin evidence since gateway ids are not MODEL_PINS candidates. Add modelFamily(ref) so the §6.1 separation check compares vendor families, not serving providers.
consequences: Paper names Mistral Medium 3.5 with the I7 rule as reason. All judge traffic on one gateway account; the pin removes routing non-determinism. Dry-run $14.32 list for 1,428 calls with all three priced. Reversible by funding direct keys; verdict stores are per judge slug so nothing judged is lost.
reversible: yes - fund direct xAI/Mistral keys and restore the direct refs; judgments are stored per judge slug

title: Rubric v2: the judge items are revised after G8a fell below the floor on every dimension
context: The 2026-09-20 calibration pass (ADR-0032) put judge-vs-self kappa below the G8 floor of 0.6 on every dimension (factuality 0.345, compliance 0.454, salesEffectiveness 0.454, conversationQuality -0.003; anchors FA1 0.41, SA1 0.29, SA2 0.36, QA1 0.07) and the reversed-order ablation breached the 0.10 flip threshold on salesEffectiveness (0.211) and on the anchors (0.254). Master Plan §8/§11 mandate a rubric rewrite below 0.6 and a redesign below 0.4 before any score is published. A three-way audit on 2026-09-21 (protocol/ADR conformance, code and tests, and a replay of every proposed rule against the 119 self labels) shaped the revision; several first-draft rules were dropped because the replay showed they contradicted the human key or the pre-registered design.
decision: data/judge-items.json goes 1.3.0 -> 2.0.0 with no item added, removed or renumbered. Interpretation notes: F1 treats a wrongly combined or double-counted figure as unsupported and requires totals to be recomputed (numeric self-contradiction stays F4); CP3 covers mis-computed totals with stated boundaries against CP4/CP5/CP6/CP11; CP9 mirrors the deterministic check L1.9 exactly; SE1/SE2 need asked AND answered or explicitly refused, OR volunteered and confirmed back (the confirmed-back limb is kept: dropping it creates the buyer-dependent denominator D2 forbids); SE4 needs a volunteered requirement confirmed back or used to filter; SE5 keeps both a SECURED and an ATTEMPTED branch, both sharpened, superseding ADR-0026's SE5 wording while keeping its principle; CQ1 is a chunking rule with no length threshold; CQ3 gets positive failure criteria led by capability denial, with ADR-0029's exclusions intact. FA1 and SA2 change in scale and example text (notes render only for binary items); SA2 gains level-1 and level-2 examples because no judge used level 1. The shared output contract gains constant format lines (each id once, only shown keys, mandatory anchors block, no turn key), so the prompt hash changes and v1 verdicts are archived to calibration/archive/v1-2026-09-20/. Every verdict, meta pass file and label file carries itemsVersion; agreement/ablation/gate readers throw on mixed promptSha or itemsVersion within one (judge, dimension) and skip archived* folders. Advisory evidenceMeta flag beside evidenceFound (never a schema violation, per ADR-0019); raw judge reply stored on structured errors. Seeded sidecars gain a precision-only alsoCovered list while violatedItems stays the G9 recall authority (ADR-0025). Human labels are not re-done wholesale: about 27 positions are re-checked under v2 and the prior folder is archived. Unchanged: composite weights, D1/D4/D7, the ablation set and thresholds, QA1 text, panel composition, judgeApplicability.
consequences: All four dimensions are re-judged (about the cost of the first pass, roughly $25-30 metered) once a dedicated OpenRouter key exists, the reversed-order 50-slice pass is re-run, and agreement, seeded recall and flip rates are recomputed; no v1 number carries forward. The paper reports v1 and v2 kappa side by side plus the anchor flip-rate breach so the published figure is never best-of. Colleague raters get the slice under v2 text only. Widening the CP3 hard-fail after seeing disagreements is disclosed as post-hoc, with seeded recall recomputed. Re-running pnpm checks on the calibration sweeps (ADR-0024) remains outstanding before Phase 6.
reversible: yes - v1 verdicts and the pre-recheck labels are archived, data/judge-items.json is versioned, and the readers refuse to mix versions

title: Maverick judge re-pinned from DeepInfra to Novita after DeepInfra was delisted; transport failures are no longer persisted as verdicts
context: Resuming the rubric v2 calibration pass on 2026-10-14, every call to openrouter/meta-llama/llama-4-maverick@DeepInfra failed before billing: DeepInfra no longer serves the model on OpenRouter and the ADR-0016 pin disallows fallbacks. The runner also persisted each transport failure (call_failed) as a verdict file, 351 of them, which every later resume would have skipped and the agreement reader would have scored as judge errors.
decision: Re-pin the Maverick slot to Novita (fp8, 1M context, $0.27/$0.85, the closest match to the DeepInfra serving) and rerun the whole Maverick v2 pass there (476 primary + 200 reversed) so every Maverick verdict comes from one host; archive the 325 partial DeepInfra verdicts and the 351 call_failed files under calibration/archive/. The runner no longer writes a verdict file for call_failed; it counts it as callFailed in the meta pass and retries it on resume, while no_json and schema_violation stay persisted. The Maverick price row moves to Novita before any Novita call. ADR-0032 stands for Grok and Mistral and is not edited.
consequences: The v1-vs-v2 Maverick agreement comparison changes rubric and serving host at once and must be reported that way; Grok and Mistral are single-variable. Pinned hosts can be delisted again, so panel endpoints are re-checked before every paid pass. A schema violation followed by a transport-failed retry is re-judged rather than counted, a small accepted undercount. Session spend reconciled to the cent ($17.1478 metered vs $17.1478 key usage). Follow-up: meta pass file names collide when two per-judge processes start in the same second.

title: The buyer simulator sees only the trap modules a scenario arms
context: activeTrapIds is defined as the subset of a persona's traps armed in a scenario, and ADR-0015, the G6 audit view and every scenario's ground truth assume unarmed traps stay silent, but buildBuyerSystemPrompt rendered persona.hidden whole. 33 of 113 public scenarios bound a persona with an unarmed trap; 20 of those expect a site visit or a logged qualification, and a correct escalation in reply to a sprung trap ends the flow and fails L1.5 (11 scenarios) or L1.6 (2). Three author notes on P03 and P11 also named the trap mechanism in every scenario.
decision: Render hidden.traps filtered to activeTrapIds, keeping key order so fully-armed and trap-free scenarios render byte-identical prompts. Remove the three trap-naming author clauses and bump P03 and P11 to 1.1.0. Scope is trap modules only: character fields that motivate trap-like asks (chiefly P11) and scenario opening messages are left as they are.
consequences: Buyer prompt sha changes for 37 public scenarios (33 exposed plus fully-armed P03/P11), pre-Phase 6; the per-scenario buyerPromptSha256 in sweep manifests is the comparability key. The Phase 3 pilot and calibration sweeps keep their recorded behaviour, and L1.5/L1.6 misses after a correct escalation to an unarmed trap are a known artefact there. The G6 audit server rebuilds prompts from current code, so the recorded sha is the reference for older runs. The Phase 6 G6 spot-check counts unarmed-trap springs from character pressure separately from scripted openers.
